RETRIEVAL -- the publisher PDF at https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/ielx7/7333/10031624/09991178.pdf, which both Unpaywall and Semantic Scholar give as the open-access location, returns a JavaScript challenge page under HTTP 200 (15 KB of HTML). The working endpoint is https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stampPDF/getPDF.jsp?tp=&arnumber=9991178&ref= with a browser user-agent, which returns the real 2.5 MB PDF; the %PDF header was checked before the file was kept. Recording this because IEEE was not in the collection-practice list of publishers that block automated fetches. EXTRACTION -- pymupdf4llm, per _briefs/collection-practice.md; markitdown was not used. md_quality: partial, which is a stronger statement than the two-column 'rough' default and is deliberate: Tables I, II, III and IV are embedded in the PDF as images with no text layer at all, so no converter could recover them. Confirmed by running pymupdf get_text over page 6, which returns the table captions and nothing between them. What this loses is every accuracy number in the paper: the per-subject and average results on BCI Competition IV 2a and 2b and on SEED, and the convolution-module layer table. Those numbers were recovered by rendering pages 4, 6 and 7 of the committed source.pdf to PNG at 200 dpi and reading them, and the values quoted on the card (Conformer 78.66 / kappa 0.7155 on Dataset I, 84.63 / 0.6926 on Dataset II, 95.30 / 0.9295 on Dataset III, with the EEGNet, ConvNet, FBCSP, C2CM, FBCNet, DRDA, SVM, GELM, DGCNN, R2G-STNN and RGNN comparators) come from that reading of the archived PDF, not from source.md. The parameter count quoted on the card as roughly 0.79 million is read off the right-hand axis of Fig. 4 in the same way and is stated on the card as a figure reading rather than a reported value. Running prose, the ablation and parameter-sensitivity sections, the discussion and the reference list all extract faithfully.
